page: Amazon Web Services inf2.xlarge is a virtualized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor operating at a clock speed of 3.6 GHz. The instance is configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. It includes 16.0 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, which provides 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The processor features 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 8 MB of L3 cache, alongside support for AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI instruction sets. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark evaluations indicate a split performance profile. The single-core CPU performance is strong, placing in the top 25% in stress-ng testing, while the single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression benchmarks fall into the average category. However, multi-core CPU performance and multi-threaded decompression are weak, ranking in the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth tests for both small cached blocks and large uncached blocks also register in the bottom 25%. For specialized tasks, the instance achieves average scores in Geekbench single-core and text processing, but falls into the bottom 25% for ray tracing, image processing, and software compilation.

In terms of workload execution, the inf2.xlarge demonstrates average performance for small-model LLM text generation but drops to weak or poor performance when processing prompts or handling larger 7B parameter models. Database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput are also positioned in the bottom 25%. Given the dedicated CPU allocation and balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this instance is qualitatively suited for general-purpose workloads, light single-threaded processing, and basic application hosting where high multi-core throughput or local storage is not required.
description: Amazon Web Services inf2.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual server instance running on the Nitro hypervisor. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor with an x86_64 architecture, it provides 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores at 3.6 GHz, paired with 16.0 GB of DDR4 RAM. The instance lacks local storage and dedicated GPUs, relying on a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Performance benchmarks show strong single-core CPU capabilities, ranking in the top 25%, though multi-core performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations fall into the bottom 25%. Large-model inference and multi-threaded tasks also show weak performance. This resource profile makes the instance best suited for general-purpose workloads, single-threaded applications, and lightweight web serving where dedicated CPU allocation is required without the need for high multi-core density or local storage.
